CreateLeaveBalanceDto and CreateBalanceAdjustmentDto shape validation passes (all required fields present, optional fields correctly typed)

constraints: All database access must go through repository interfaces (GP-001) — the repository interfaces defined in this phase are the contract for all future DB access
Strict TypeScript: no implicit any, strict null checks — all interface fields must use explicit types, nullable fields use `| null` not optional chaining alone
remainingDays must be derived (totalEntitlement - usedDays), never stored independently (BR-002 from ARCHITECTURE.md)
Module files follow the naming convention: src/modules/balance/balance.{model,repository}.ts
outOfScope: Database migrations (Phase 2) — leave_balances and balance_adjustments tables
Balance service interface and implementation (Phase 4) — IBalanceService, BalanceService with applyAdjustment business logic
Balance controller (Phase 5) and routes (Phase 6) — HTTP layer
Module barrel export and app registration (Phase 7)
Audit logging (GP-002), RBAC enforcement (GP-005), input validation at API boundaries (GP-003) — no state-changing operations or endpoints in this phase
LeaveBalanceStatus.CANCELLED and BalanceAdjustmentStatus.FAILED — present in ARCHITECTURE.md full design but deferred beyond Phase 1

ambiguities.description: LeaveBalance interface declares remainingDays as a "derived" field (totalEntitlement - usedDays), but TypeScript interfaces cannot express computed/derived properties. The code-agent must decide: (a) define it as a readonly property with the derivation enforced at construction time, (b) use a class with a getter, or (c) export a pure function `computeRemainingDays(balance)`. The test only verifies the arithmetic, not the mechanism.
options: Define remainingDays as a readonly property set at construction via factory function
Use a LeaveBalance class with a getter for remainingDays
Export a standalone computeRemainingDays(totalEntitlement, usedDays) utility function
